correctness.rationale: The four nonzero Möbius terms give z^t(1-z^{t(p-1)})(1-H(z^t)), where H has q positive unit coefficients at exponents q-1+j(p-1). The constant term of the last two factors is 1, establishing origin multiplicity t; the middle factor contributes only unit-modulus roots. For H(z)=1, monotonicity of H(r) gives the unique positive radius and the lower bound. Equality forces every phase to be 1, and the first two consecutive exponents force exactly the gcd subgroup; zH'(z) is then a strictly positive sum. The nonzero t-th-root map is unramified, giving tg simple boundary roots. The raw radii vary with t, as the explicit t-th-root formula specifies; the squarefree kernel determines the parent moduli, not identical radii for all powers. For the fixed-p estimate, u=-(q-1)log rho lies between log(q)/p and log(q). The exact geometric series gives e^{-u}=(1-e^{-(p-1)u/(q-1)})/(1-e^{-q(p-1)u/(q-1)}), so e^{-u}=O_p(log q/q), and the denominator differs from 1 by at most that order. Therefore u+log u=log((q-1)/(p-1))+O_p(log q/q); the inverse is 1-Lipschitz there, and expanding 1-e^{-u/(q-1)} yields the stated error.
